rules.title: CPD Policy 423 — Public Recording of Law Enforcement Activity
rules.summary: Affirmatively recognizes lawful recording of officers performing official duties and directs officers not to prohibit or intentionally interfere with lawful recording. It separates recording alone from interference.
rules.constitutional_test: First Amendment recording doctrine + lawful-vantage/noninterference limits
rules.enforcement_hook: Policy itself constrains officer response; other enforcement requires independent legal basis.
open_questions: Exact application to privacy-sensitive lobby subjects remains fact-specific.

rules.title: CPD Policy 803 — Records Unit
rules.summary: Requires secure handling/access controls for police records. It governs department custody of records and is not by itself a rule forbidding ordinary lobby patrons from operating cameras.
rules.constitutional_test: Use as privacy/security interest; any patron restriction must be separately sourced and tested.
open_questions: What counter-layout/signage safeguards implement this policy at the public Records counter?

rules.title: CPD Policy 806 — Protected Information
rules.summary: Creates department-side handling/access obligations for protected information. It does not create a building-wide public camera prohibition.
rules.constitutional_test: Specific exposed information + actual visitor rule + NPF reasonableness/viewpoint neutrality.
open_questions: Any public-facing derivative rule or sign based on this policy?

rules.title: CPD Policy 422 — Body-Worn Cameras
rules.summary: Officer-side BWC policy distinguishes ordinary official recording from certain private/confidential contexts. It is useful privacy-comparator evidence, not a patron-camera rule.
rules.constitutional_test: Context evidence only; public restriction must be independently sourced.

rules.title: Community Meeting Room Use Restrictions / Contract
rules.summary: City publicly opens the room to qualifying nonprofit community groups for community/quality-of-life discussion, subject to restrictions and a contract. The full current contract was not located online.
open_questions: Obtain complete current contract and incorporated restrictions.

rules.title: California Penal Code §148(g) — Recording Officers
applies_to: recording public/peace officers where statutory location condition is met
rules.summary: Provides that recording an officer, by itself, does not constitute §148(a) obstruction and does not by itself create reasonable suspicion or probable cause when the statutory location condition is satisfied.
rules.constitutional_test: Statutory protection layered on First Amendment recording doctrine.
rules.enforcement_hook: Limits use of §148(a), reasonable suspicion, and probable cause based on recording alone.
open_questions: Independent conduct beyond recording must still be analyzed.

rules.title: California Penal Code §632 — Confidential Communications
rules.summary: May directly regulate audio recording where objective confidentiality and statutory elements are present. It does not make all police-lobby audio confidential.
rules.enforcement_hook: Penal Code §632 where elements are met.
open_questions: Which lobby/counter interactions objectively qualify as confidential?

rules.title: California Penal Code §602.1 — Public-Agency/Business Obstruction and Savings Clause
rules.summary: The statewide public-agency interference framework is now researched. Facility application still depends on the actual conduct, request to leave, and statutory elements.
rules.constitutional_test: Protected activity → savings clause → additional obstruction/intimidation conduct → refusal → enforcement
rules.enforcement_hook: Penal Code §602.1 where elements are met.
open_questions: What CPD training or local practice governs §602.1 in public-lobby recording encounters?

rules.title: California Penal Code §602 — Trespass
rules.summary: The statewide trespass framework is now researched as subsection-specific. Facility application still depends on access status, the basis and scope of any exclusion, and the later conduct.
rules.constitutional_test: Exact subsection/elements + lawful exclusion + constitutional limits
rules.enforcement_hook: Only the applicable §602 subsection, if any.
open_questions: Which subsection is used by CPD for public-lobby refusal-to-leave scenarios?

rules.title: Concord Municipal Code ch. 9.08 — Solicitation Location Restrictions
rules.summary: The citywide ordinance prohibits solicitation in public parking lots/structures and within 30 feet of a queue of five or more persons, among other places. It may affect the Police Headquarters public parking/approach only where the exact location falls within the ordinance. Its constitutionality must be analyzed area-by-area rather than inferred from the ordinance's own findings.
rules.constitutional_test: California Speech Clause + federal forum/time-place-manner analysis mapped to the exact Police property subarea
rules.enforcement_hook: Infraction; repeated violations may be charged as a misdemeanor under the ordinance.
open_questions: Whether the Headquarters public parking/approach is treated as a 'public parking lot' under the ordinance.
Whether passive signs or responses to inquiries fall outside the ordinance's definition of solicitation.

cpra_targets.target: Any internal Concord Police Headquarters visitor/security directive, post order, roll-call bulletin, training, or supervisor guidance governing public recording, observation, solicitation, privacy, or information gathering in the lobby, Records counter, entrance, or public parking/approach.
cpra_targets.why: Policy 423 is public and protective; the key remaining question is whether narrower unpublished headquarters rules exist and how they are reconciled with Policy 423 and §148(g).

cpra_targets.target: Current lobby/Records/entrance signage orders, templates, installation records, and policy source for camera, phone, privacy, identification, waiting, solicitation, or restricted-area signs.
cpra_targets.why: The public-source sweep still cannot establish what is physically posted or the authority behind any sign.

cpra_targets.target: Training/guidance on Policy 423, Penal Code §§148, 602, and 602.1, including removal/exclusion of persons recording or refusing to stop recording in public-facing areas.
cpra_targets.why: Needed to test whether actual training preserves the distinction between protected recording and independent interference/trespass predicates.

cpra_targets.target: Incidents/complaints during the last three years involving public recording in the Headquarters lobby or Records counter, including CAD, body-worn-camera, incident reports, cited policy, and disposition.
cpra_targets.why: Would reveal actual application, comparator treatment, and any conflict between Policy 423 and local practice.

cpra_targets.target: Current complete Police Department Community Meeting Room contract and incorporated use restrictions if it cannot be obtained through ordinary public web channels.
cpra_targets.why: The room is a distinct LPF channel and the complete terms remain a public-source gap.
